subject: Warm pool & autoscale SLO follow-up (latency targets + scale-up behavior)
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightanalytics.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@brightanalytics.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Warm pool & autoscale SLO follow-up (latency targets + scale-up behavior)

Hi Alyssa / Mateo —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap so we’re all aligned and to put the next steps on the calendar. Please reply if I missed anything.

Call highlights:
- BrightAnalytics will target a 95th-percentile tail latency of <= 220ms for single-stream inference at peak traffic.
- Typical steady-state concurrency: ~180 qps across 3 regional endpoints; burst events expected up to 2.5x for 5–10 minute windows (~450 qps).
- Streaming: client requires incremental token streaming for long responses (average 400 tokens), with per-chunk latency under 80ms.

Open technical questions we flagged (action owners in parentheses):
1) Cold scale-up time for a new GPU shard (cold-start, from 0 GPUs to full service) — target must be <90s (Rafael).
2) Warm-pool sizing and pre-warmed slots — suggested initial warm pool = 30% of expected peak concurrency (Sofia + SE review).
3) Queueing/backpressure behavior when all active workers are saturated — prefer graceful 429-with-retry-after vs unbounded queueing (BrightAnalytics preference) (Alyssa).
4) Streaming chunk sizing and whether KV cache priming affects first-token latency (Rafael).

Attachments included: MAP-BrightAnalytics-v1.pdf (mutual action plan), warm_pool_diagram.png (concept diagram). I dropped an initial warm-pool sizing calc in the MAP — please scan.

Proposed next steps:
- Rafael to provide scale-up and warm-pool timing estimates and recommended pre-warm percentage (by EOD Wed PT).
- Alma (BrightAnalytics) to confirm acceptance of 429 behavior vs queueing (Alyssa to confirm).
- Sofia to share a scoped warm-pool trial proposal and pricing impact (this thread).

Would you be available for a 30-min follow-up on Thu 11/12 or Fri 11/13 to review Rafael’s numbers and agree the trial?

Best,
Sofia
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightanalytics.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@brightanalytics.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Warm pool & autoscale SLO follow-up (latency targets + scale-up behavior)

Thanks Sofia — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 95p <= 220ms target is specifically for inference-only time measured at our edge (post-auth, pre-aggregation). If pre- and post-processing are counted, +30–40ms is expected; can Redwood provide both raw inference and end-to-end measurements?
- For streaming, the 80ms per-chunk SLO is for token availability at the client level. If there’s unavoidable jitter during scale-up (e.g., first chunk slower), we need an SLA-friendly fallback path.

Regarding queueing behavior: we prefer a short queued window (<= 5s) with an explicit Retry-After header rather than immediate 429s for transient bursts. If warm-pool slots can be prebooked and we can observe predictable scale-up times, a 5s queue aligns with our front-end retry policy.

We’re flexible on the follow-up; Thu 11/12 11:00am PT works for Mateo and me.

—Alyssa
Senior Platform PM | BrightAnalytics

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightanalytics.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@brightanalytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Warm pool & autoscale SLO follow-up (latency targets + scale-up behavior)

Hi all — digging into specifics from the call and Alyssa’s notes. Below is a conservative, data-driven set of expectations based on the model family you plan to use (Llama-3-34B equivalent) and our typical cold/warm behaviors on the instance types you selected.

Quick summary (numbers are median ± variance ranges):
- Cold scale-up (0 -> accept traffic, full kernel load): 65–95s (median 78s) — includes container startup, kernel JIT where applicable, and model weights staged from local SSDs.
- Warm-pool slot activation (pre-warmed process, weights resident): 4–9s (median 6s). This assumes we keep a pre-warmed process with KV cache primed for recent prefixes — warm-pool cost is higher but provides the lower activation latency.
- Per-token steady-state tail latency (95p) running on warm slot: 160–210ms (fits your 220ms SLO with headroom).
- Streaming first-chunk penalty (when bringing up new shards): first chunk may see +120–200ms overhead vs steady-state; subsequent chunks stabilize.

Queueing behavior options we support (configurable per-route):
1) Short in-process queue (max wait <= 5s) with Retry-After header when delay exceeds threshold — fits your front-end retry plan.
2) Immediate 429 with client-side retry guidance (lower server-side memory footprint).
3) Hybrid: accept into a bounded queue for up to 3s, then 429 (middle ground).

Recommended initial config for trial:
- Warm-pool = 25% of observed peak concurrency (45 pre-warmed slots).
- Burst tolerance: allow bounded queue of 5s; any requests beyond that receive 429 + Retry-After.
- Instrumentation: export both inference-time and end-to-end timings to your observability (we can forward per-request traces to your Datadog/Prometheus endpoint).

I attached a simple CSV with simulated scale scenarios (scale-metrics-20261110.csv) and an updated warm_pool_diagram.png showing slot lifecycle. The MAP has a trial line-item we can tweak (pricing delta for 25% warm pool).

Open items:
- Confirm whether BrightAnalytics wants the hybrid or full queueing approach (Alyssa).
- Agree the trial sizing (Sofia / Alyssa).
- Approve brief SLA amendment for streaming-first-chunk jitter during shard warm-up (legal / procurement later).

Technical note: if you want sub-50ms first-token tails for long responses we need a higher pre-warm percentage or pinned hot-shards for critical routes; we can cost that out if necessary.

Regards,
Rafael
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:25:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Warm pool & autoscale SLO follow-up (latency targets + scale-up behavior) — trial ask

Ben / Monica — forwarding the thread with the call recap and Rafael’s technical breakdown. TL;DR: BrightAnalytics is asking for a 2-week warm-pool trial sized at ~25% pre-warmed slots (45 slots) with bounded queueing up to 5s. They need the trial to validate 95p latency at production concurrency and confirm streaming behavior.

Why this is a good trial:
- High signal on cost/benefit: we’ll collect per-token cost delta vs no warm pool and the real impact on end-to-end SLA.
- Sales motion: high probability expansion if steady-state and burst behavior are within the 220ms 95p target.

Requests:
1) Approval to offer a 2-week warm-pool pilot at a 50% discounted incremental warm-pool fee (standard discount play for trials) — this is an exception to the normal 25% discount cap (Ben).
2) Approval for limited SLA language acknowledging first-chunk jitter during shard warm-up (Monica / legal to sign off on the wording) so BrightAnalytics can include it in procurement docs.

If you want, Rafael and I can join a quick 15-min sync to walk the numbers and the CSV scenario outputs before any formal approval. Rafael’s recommended trial config is attached.

Thanks — aiming to convert trial into a reserved capacity deal if metrics look good.

Sofia
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
